_meta.description:
Somewhere to put an UNVERIFIED MFA secret (ADR-037 fragment). Additive only: one new optional property, nothing changes type and nothing becomes required, so the register import needs no breaking-change acknowledgement.

WHY IT HAS TO EXIST. PortalAuthController::mfaEnroll() said, in its own comment, 'stash the encrypted secret as pending until verification confirms it' -- and then wrote it to `mfaSecret`, the LIVE field, while setting `mfaEnabled = false`. There was nowhere else to put it. The effect was that calling enroll on an account with a working second factor destroyed that factor and switched MFA off, before proving anything: anyone holding a stolen password could strip the second factor and then log in with the password alone.

The secret is stored encrypted, exactly like `mfaSecret`, and is cleared on successful verification.

ON THE PROPERTY DESCRIPTION: schema descriptions are rendered as FORM HELP TEXT and are translated, so the property carries a short line a person can read. The implementation contract is here instead: written by mfaEnroll; promoted to `mfaSecret` by mfaVerify once a valid code proves the authenticator holds it; cleared on success. It is NEVER a fallback for authentication -- a code is only accepted against it DURING enrolment, never for a login, or the pending value would itself become a second factor nobody verified.

mfaPendingSecret.title: Pending MFA secret
mfaPendingSecret.description: A second factor that has been set up but not yet confirmed with a code. It never counts as a working second factor.
